feedback.end: Vesuvius is a volcano near the city of Naples in Italy. It is famous because of its eruption in AD 79.

atoms.b: During the time of the eruption, Vesuvius was above a ((subtraction ++subduction)) zone as the African Plate and Eurasian Plate were moving towards each other.
As the African Plate was forced under the Eurasian Plate, part of the African Plate melted due to the high ((distances ++temperatures)) in the mantle. Magma started to build up under Vesuvius.

instruction.text: What do you think happened after the magma began to build up?

feedback.end: The first warning signs came at 8am, when a small eruption cloud escaped the crater. By 1pm, this cloud was 20 km high!

instruction.text: Vesuvius is a composite volcano. What do you think its eruption was like?

text: Composite volcanoes have steeper sides and more explosive eruptions.

feedback.finish: The magma in Vesuvius was filled with bubbles that exploded when they reached the outside air.

b: ++Thick lava, rocks, ash and gas were launched into air.
Runny lava trickled down the volcano.
Nothing was released from the volcano.

instruction.text: How do you think nearby cities were affected by the eruption?

atoms.b: The nearby cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum were completely ((unaffected ++destroyed)) by Vesuvius as hot ash and rocks rained down on the people and buildings.
The damage worsened after the now 30-kilometre-high eruption ((ocean ++cloud)) collapsed under its own weight onto the surrounding area. Its heat turned anything it touched into ash.
The ruins of these cities were uncovered hundreds of years ((earlier ++later)) and can now be visited by tourists!
